headline: Tata Motors iRA apps found vulnerable with hardcoded credentials, high severity
summary: Multiple high-severity vulnerabilities in Tata Motors iRA and iRA.ev applications could allow attackers to obtain sensitive credentials, access vehicle information, and impersonate users, posing a significant risk to data security.
details: Multiple high-severity vulnerabilities have been identified in the Tata Motors iRA 2.0 and iRA.ev mobile applications. These flaws could grant unauthorized access to sensitive vehicle-related information and services, impacting users of both platforms.

The issues include hardcoded credentials, which attackers could exploit to gain access. This could lead to user impersonation and unauthorized modification of application data, posing a significant risk to user privacy and vehicle security.

The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) reported these vulnerabilities, assigning CVEs CVE-2026-121144, CVE-2026-121145, CVE-2026-121146, and CVE-2026-121147. The original issue date was November 4, 2026.

Users of the affected iRA 2.0 and iRA.ev mobile applications are advised to be aware of these risks. Tata Motors has been notified, and users should look out for official updates or patches to secure their applications.
caption:
High-severity vulnerabilities found in Tata Motors iRA apps. Hardcoded credentials could expose sensitive vehicle data and allow user impersonation.

Multiple high-severity vulnerabilities have been identified in the Tata Motors iRA 2.0 and iRA.ev mobile applications. These flaws could grant unauthorized access to sensitive vehicle-related information and services, impacting users of both platforms.

The issues include hardcoded credentials, which attackers could exploit to gain access. This could lead to user impersonation and unauthorized modification of application data, posing a significant risk to user privacy and vehicle security.

The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) reported these vulnerabilities, assigning CVEs CVE-2026-121144, CVE-2026-121145, CVE-2026-121146, and CVE-2026-121147. The original issue date was November 4, 2026.

Users of the affected iRA 2.0 and iRA.ev mobile applications are advised to be aware of these risks. Tata Motors has been notified, and users should look out for official updates or patches to secure their applications.
